messages.subject: gpa vs bilateral symmetry
parts:
I performed generalized Procrustes analysis on my shape data using the gpagen function. Code:

Y.gpa <- gpagen(A = avg_coords_by_species, curves= curvepts, ProcD=FALSE, Proj=TRUE)

I then enforced object symmetry on the Procrustes fit coordinates using the bilat.symmetry function. Code:

Y.sym=bilat.symmetry(Y.gpa$coords, ind = species, object.sym = TRUE, land.pairs = land.pairs, RRPP = TRUE, iter = 999, print.progress = TRUE)

When I plot the relationship of the PC axes (>99% of the variation) for Y.gpa$coords and Y.sym$symm.shape, there is a near linear relationship between them for the first 3 PCs. However, higher level PCs (5 through 8) are uncorrelated. Plots attached here. It is not immediately clear to me why this is the case. Can someone help me determine why the first three axes are nearly perfectly correlated but the others are not? Happy to provide more information if necessary.

messages.author: 511e44c7d1e1bab0
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] gpa vs bilateral symmetry
parts:
Nick,

when conducting a bilateral symmetry analysis, one of the things you obtain is the partitioning of total shape variation (from GPA) into a symmetric and asymmetric shape component. These correspond to the $sym.shape and $asym.shape parts of the output of the function. For understanding how this partitioning is done, please refer toMardia, K. V, Bookstein, F. L. & Moreton, I. J. Statistical assessment of bilateral symmetry of shapes. Biometrika 87, 285–300 (2000).

When you run a pca on Procrustes residuals (gpagen$coords), you are doing this on the total shape variation. Instead, with a pca of sym.shape you are only considering the symmetric component. This is why pca scores will never be perfectly correlated. The fact that the first pcs look highly correlated is that, in your sample (and I dare say in most biological settings), the symmetric shape component captures a large part of the total shape variation, which is reflected in the pc axes structure.

Hope this helps,

Antigoni
